- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 2-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent sentiment shifts from negative to neutral.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply 3-period exponential smoothing to dampen volatility-driven forecasts.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, correct by aligning forecast to 14-day trend unless sentiment strongly contradicts it.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 10-day average as baseline and adjust forecast toward it if sentiment is weak or neutral.
